function: DNN prediction of RIS phase shifts from the BS-RIS and RIS-user channels, plus a learned BS precoder, trained end-to-end within a semantic communication system for 3-D reconstruction (pp. 5-6).
system: Passive reflecting RIS, N=64 elements, amplitude 1; BS with M=4 UPA antennas, one single-antenna user, MISO, no direct link; DeepMIMO channel at 28 GHz (pp. 3, 6-8).
method: Transformer semantic encoder/decoder, MLP RIS-phase predictor and precoder, U-Net semantic-to-Gaussian mapper; supervised two-stage end-to-end training (MSE, then L2+LPIPS), training SNR 12 dB (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: BS-RIS: simulated Saleh-Valenzuela, 3 paths; RIS-user: DeepMIMO ray-tracing, 3 scenarios, 102,400 samples; images from ShapeNet-SRN Chair and Car (p. 8).
test_conditions: Trained at 12 dB SNR; tested from -10 to 16 dB and at 12 and -2 dB; channel train/test split not stated; ShapeNet test objects held out (pp. 8-10).
baselines: Only-RIS and only-precoding ablations; QAM+LDPC with and without RIS optimization; Splatter, SC-Splatter, SC-R-Splatter (Restormer denoising) and PixelNeRF for 3-D reconstruction (pp. 8-10).
metrics: Feature PSNR versus SNR; novel-view PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS and rendering time of 250 views (pp. 8-10).
complexity: Rendering time of 250 views: 2.08 s (ours) vs 280.30 s (PixelNeRF) on one RTX 4080 Super GPU; no parameters or FLOPs (pp. 7, 10, 11).
openness: none released; public DeepMIMO [41] and ShapeNet-SRN [40] used, no link (p. 8).
q1_support: p. 8: "publicly available DeepMIMO dataset [41]" is used for the RIS-to-user channel (the BS-RIS channel is Saleh-Valenzuela, a custom model).
q2_support: p. 8: "channel samples are randomly selected and fully traversed within each validation epoch"; training SNR is 12 dB (Table I) and testing sweeps the SNR (Fig. 5), which does not count. Missing: any held-out scenario, band or site.
q3_support: p. 10: "PixelNeRF takes the original GT image as input" (Splatter also uses GT input, p. 9), so both are reconstruction references, not learned RIS or precoding baselines; the non-learned baseline is QAM+LDPC with and without RIS optimization (p. 9); ablations do not count. Missing: any earlier learned RIS-phase or precoding method.
q4_support: p. 11: "our method completes the task in only 2 s"; Table III (p. 10) lists Time(s) 2.08 for the proposed method (rendering of 250 views). No parameters or FLOPs are reported.
q5_support: p. 8: "publicly available DeepMIMO dataset [41]" is used for the RIS-to-user channel; no code or data link of its own is given.
notes: Included as area 3: DNN RIS phase prediction and BS precoding are learned end-to-end inside a semantic communication system (pp. 5-6); semantic coding alone would not count. For the reviewer, q1 rests on DeepMIMO for the RIS-user link only; the BS-RIS link is a Saleh-Valenzuela simulation (p. 8). q2: p. 9 claims 'generalization capability', but the paper never states that a scenario, band or site was held out of training; only the SNR varies (training 12 dB, Table I). q3: no earlier learned RIS or precoding method is compared; Splatter and PixelNeRF are 3-D reconstruction models run on ground-truth images; the reviewer may judge differently. q4: only the rendering time of 250 views is reported (Table III), not parameters, FLOPs or the cost of the RIS predictor; marked met as a measured runtime of the proposed system. The text extraction omits Tables I-III; they were read from the page images (pp. 8, 10).
